end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from where it is grown or made to home.
Identified local food as having fewer food miles.
Compared nearby and distant foods: distant food uses more fuel and nearby food is fresher.
Explained that refrigeration can increase electricity use.
Used arrow length to represent travel distance; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and comparing local and distant foods. They used the method of linking a longer journey with more fuel and explained that refrigeration can use more electricity. Rohan also connected nearby food with freshness and described arrow length as travel distance. At home, ask them to compare two foods and name which travelled farther, then give one effect on fuel, pollution, or freshness.
